catalog_quote: Le luri distingue six timbres vocaliques, avec une opposition de longueur : i/ii; u/uu; e/ee; Œ/ŒŒ; o/oo; a/aa. Le système consonantique tel qu'on le devine dans ces quelques notes est typique des langues SBW. ... Le système tonal comprend deux niveaux : Bas et Haut. Dans la transcription, le ton haut est noté par un accent aigu (á et áá), le ton tombant par un accent circonflexe (â), et le ton bas n'est pas noté (a et aa). L'enquête succincte qui été réalisée n'a pas fait apparaître de ton montant.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.translation: The tonal system comprises two levels: Low and High. In the transcription, high tone is marked with an acute accent (á and áá), falling tone with a circumflex (â), and low tone is not marked (a and aa). The brief survey that was carried out did not reveal any rising tone.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Luri is described as a two-level tone language (Low, High, plus a falling contour on long/heavy syllables); lexical items carry tone in the wordlist. The source says nothing about word stress or accentual prominence, so no stress rule can be stated.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the author stresses the data are extremely limited (about two hours of elicitation with the last speaker, aged over 80, via a Hausa questionnaire).
new_statements.domain_note: Citation forms (about 200 lexical items) and a handful of short elicited sentences; tone marked on words. No prosodic/phrase-level description.
new_statements.identity_note: Luri [luri1256, ISO ldd] = Lúr, a village about 15 km SE of Bauchi near Langas, Bauchi LGA, Bauchi State, Nigeria; South Bauchi West (Polci cluster, Glottolog subgroup 'Polci-Luri' nyam1284). Caron 2004, the only first-hand description, is based on about two hours with the last two speakers (2001-2002) and concludes that Luri is 'vraisemblablement une seule et même langue' with Nyamzak (Langas), now ISO nzr Nyamzak-Dir-Mbarimi after the 2023 split of plj. Blench 2020 gives '2 (Caron 2002)' speakers and 'probably extinct (2016)'. Note: the polc1243 held by the project cites the Luri glottocode as 'luri1259'; the Glottolog record downloaded here confirms luri1256 (luri125x codes for Iranian Luri are unrelated).

sources.note: Sec. 1 'Phonologie' (preprint p.2, HAL PDF p.3): six vowel qualities with a length contrast, consonants 'typique des langues SBW', and 'Le systeme tonal comprend deux niveaux : Bas et Haut' with high tone marked by acute, falling by circumflex, low unmarked; no rising tone found. Nothing at all about stress/accent (the word 'accent' occurs only as the names of tone diacritics). Data = about two hours with the last speaker, Musa (>80), 2001-2002; Caron says Luri and Nyamzak are probably one and the same language.
